title: sub: p1-tool-runtime
creator: codex
notes: S1 done (PR #591). S2 done (PR #592). S3a/b/c-1/c-2/d done (PR #593-#597): every direct tool call in backend/agents/** is gone. S4 (this branch): the L1 tool-schema layer finally has a producer (backend/tools/runtime/schema.py + bridge.tool_schema_section, which goes through the subset() seam S1 reserved for exactly this), reached through RunContext.tool_schema and seeded by the compiler, with per-agent declarations (BaseAgent.tool_capabilities). The layer is OFF by default (BaseAgent.include_tool_schema = False) -- a deliberate deviation from the ticket's 'refresh the baseline snapshot', confirmed with the user before implementing: the model has no tool-calling channel until P2c, so listing capabilities would describe an ability it cannot exercise and invite tool-call syntax in its JSON output, while costing tokens on every request. Result: all 14 prompts byte-identical, baseline drift 0. Flipping the flag per agent is P2c's call. The renderer branches on pass_style (S1's hand-off: a MAPPING tool's single `data` parameter must not read like the nine that unpack by name) and deliberately omits side_effect/auth_scope/latency/cost -- L1 describes the call shape, not the runtime's authority over the call. An unknown capability raises rather than being silently dropped, because 'off by default' means nothing would notice the misconfiguration. Residues: L1 parameter types are reflected as found (JSON-schema 'string' vs annotation 'dict[str, Any]') with no normalisation, and params/scope/routing are declared for xhs.publish which no agent calls yet (P2a). Next: S5 (AST gate for backend/agents/** + declaration<->code agreement + coverage gate + docs/tool-runtime.md).
